findings.evidence: `GeneratorInvariance.lean:62` proves only `generator_map` for `s : ℝ≥0`, while `GeneratorInvariance.lean:72` adds only `realOperator_mem_domain`; the surrounding API uses real-time shims extensively (`Basic.lean:137` `realOperator_add`, `Basic.lean:423` `realOperator_continuousWithinAt`, and `Generator.lean:149` `generator_tendsto` is formulated with `S.realOperator`).
findings.fix: Add a theorem such as `realOperator_generator_map (S) {s : ℝ} (hs : 0 ≤ s) (x : S.domain) : S.generator ⟨S.realOperator s x, by rw [S.generator_domain]; exact S.realOperator_mem_domain hs x.property⟩ = S.realOperator s (S.generator ⟨x, by rw [S.generator_domain]; exact x.property⟩)`, derived from `generator_map` via `Real.coe_toNNReal`.
findings.issue: `realOperator_mem_domain` gives the real-time form of `map_mem_domain`, but there is no corresponding real-time form of `generator_map`, leaving users of the existing `realOperator` API without the paired identity `A (S.realOperator s x) = S.realOperator s (A x)` for `0 ≤ s`.

summary: The native `ℝ≥0` statements are at the right level, but the real-time shim API is incomplete: it exposes domain invariance without the matching commutation theorem.
